title: Reading the Cloud Path: the Hop View and Command Line View, tunnels, protocols, edges, and the error messages

prose.text: The Cloud Path view is the console's rendering of a Cloud Path probe's route; the probe itself is defined in [[zdx.probes]]. {{path-view}} {{command-line-view}}

path-view.statement: The Cloud Path view has a graph of latency or packet loss for a time period and a Hop View and Command Line View of the path from the user's device to the application or destination; selecting a point in the graph updates the path shown.

quotes: A graph that shows latency or packet loss for a particular time period.
A Hop View and Command Line View that detail the path from the user's device to the application or destination.
Select a point to update the path tracked from the device to the application.

command-line-view.statement: The Command Line View gives each hop's direction (client to egress, Public or Private Service Edge back to egress, Service Edges to destination), region and geolocation, packet loss percentage, packets failed and latency, with error icons beside IP addresses.

quotes: including the Hop Direction (probe direction, from the client to your egress IP ↓, from Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge to your egress IP ↑, and from Service Edges to destination ↓)
Region and Geolocation, Packet Loss (%) and Packets Failed, as well as Latency metrics. If there are any errors, they are indicated by an icon next to the IP address.

hop-latency.statement: The Hop View shows differential latency per leg with the highest-latency leg in orange; the latency over a Public Service Edge is between the Public Service Edge and the first router in the Zscaler data center and might indicate congestion.

quotes: Differential latency is shown over the different legs of the Cloud Path, and the leg with the highest latency displays in orange.

The latency shown on top of the Public Service Edge represents the network latency between the Public Service Edge and the first router in the Zscaler Data Center. This might indicate Public Service Edge congestion.

hop-tunnels.statement: The Hop View shows traffic through the tunnels the configured policies apply: for GRE it shows the underlay hops for more accurate latency and packet loss, and for an Internet & SaaS Private Service Edge on a private network with a private IP it shows the path from the client to the Private Service Edge.

quotes: You can see the flow of traffic through the applicable tunnels as per the configured policies.
For GRE tunnels, the Hop View displays underlay hops in the routing path to provide more accurate metrics for latency and packet loss.

In cases where the Private Service Edge for Internet & SaaS is on a private network (such as a VPN) with a private IP address, the Hop View provides a path from the client to the Private Service Edge.

tunnel-types.statement: A client reaches the Internet & SaaS Public Service Edge by Z-Tunnel 1.0 or Z-Tunnel 2.0, or by a location tunnel such as GRE or IPSec; the tunnel information lists GRE and IPSec tunnels and Z-Tunnel 1.0 or 2.0 over GRE or IPSec, and a Direct Request bypasses the tunnel and shows no tunnel graphic in the Hop View.

quotes: The client connects to the Public Service Edge for Internet & SaaS using Zscaler Tunnel (Z-Tunnel) 1.0 or Z-Tunnel 2.0.
The client connects using a location tunnel such as GRE or IPSec.
- GRE Tunnel
- IPSec Tunnel
- Z-Tunnel 1.0 over IPSec
- Z-Tunnel 1.0 over GRE
- Z-Tunnel 2.0 over GRE
- Z-Tunnel 2.0 over IPSec
If the client connects to an application using a Direct Request, then this situation indicates the client bypasses the tunnel and goes directly to the application.
In this situation, no tunnel graphic is displayed in the Hop View because there is no tunnel information to view.

citrix-proxy.statement: With Citrix as the network interface for TCP or UDP probes, ZDX shows the path to the VPN Concentrator, including traffic from the concentrator to the Public Service Edge over GRE or IPSec; with an External Proxy detected in the path, the Hop View supports several proxy topologies.

quotes: When Citrix is the network interface for TCP or UDP probes, ZDX displays the path to the VPN Concentrator.
ZDX also supports the topology where traffic from the VPN Concentrator flows to the Public Service Edge via a GRE/IPSec tunnel.
When an External Proxy is detected in the path, the Cloud Path supports several proxy topologies within the Hop View.

interface-icons.statement: Network interface types that are neither Wi-Fi nor Ethernet show a cellular (SIM card), Bluetooth or USB icon above the client icon in the Hop View, or an unknown-type icon when the type cannot be detected; geolocation and the Zscaler location are shown for the device, and geolocation is also shown for the Zscaler node in both the Hop View and the Command Line View.

quotes: Network interface types that are neither Wi-Fi nor Ethernet are indicated with one of the following icons above the client icon () in the Hop View:
Cellular (SIM card) () network type
Bluetooth () network type
USB () network type
If the network type cannot be detected, the icon for an unknown network type () is displayed.
Geolocation information and the Zscaler location are displayed for the device, and geolocation information is also displayed for the Zscaler node in both the Hop View and the Command Line View.

edges-in-path.statement: For an internet application the path shows any Public Service Edge for Internet & SaaS or for Private Access in it; for a private application it runs from Client Connector to the Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge for Private Access, and when a path is configured through the Public Service Edge for Internet & SaaS both edges appear; both views show a 4-digit internal hash for the Internet & SaaS or Private Access Public Service Edge that helps Zscaler Support.

quotes: When accessing an internet application, you can see the path from Zscaler Client Connector to the application, and if there is a Public Service Edge for Internet & SaaS or Public Service Edge for Private Access in the path, that is also displayed.
If a private application is accessed, you can view the path from Zscaler Client Connector to the Public Service Edge for Private Access or Private Service Edge for Private Access.

In case you have configured a path for traffic through the Public Service Edge for Internet & SaaS, both the Public Service Edge for Internet & SaaS and the Public Service Edge for Private Access or the Private Service Edge for Private Access are seen in the Cloud Path.

Both views display a 4-digit number for the Public Service Edge for Internet & SaaS or Public Service Edge for Private Access. This internal hash value helps Zscaler Support quickly locate and troubleshoot any issues.

leg-protocol.statement: Both views show the protocol per leg: ICMP, TCP or UDP as selected, or under Adaptive mode the protocol each leg used, with legs grouped by tunnel type also showing their protocol; Adaptive mode is not supported for internal applications through Private Access, for which only ICMP, TCP and UDP are supported.

quotes: Both views display the protocol used over the different legs of the Cloud Path. If ICMP, TCP, or UDP was selected, it is displayed in the Cloud Path. If Adaptive mode was selected, the protocol used for the different legs of the Cloud Path is displayed.
Adaptive mode is not supported for internal applications through Private Access. Only ICMP, TCP, and UDP are supported.
For Adaptive probes, legs that are grouped according to tunnel type also show their corresponding protocol.

sipa.statement: For traffic routed to an internal or external destination through Internet & SaaS Source IP Anchoring, the Cloud Path detects network issues (latencies, packet loss, jitter) and shows a path with full end-to-end visibility; the feature is in Limited Availability and enabled by contacting Zscaler Support.

quotes: When the traffic is configured for routing to an internal or external destination through Internet & SaaS Source IP Anchoring (SIPA), the Cloud Path detects any network issues (latencies, packet loss, jitter) and displays a path with full end-to-end visibility.
This feature is in Limited Availability. To enable this feature, contact Zscaler Support.

ipv6.statement: When a test target resolves to an IPv6 address, ZDX traces the end-to-end path and measures latency, packet loss and jitter across each IPv6 hop; ZDX shows dual-stack or IPv6-only configurations, relies on Internet & SaaS to route and inspect IPv6 for clients inside a location and on Client Connector for clients outside one, and the configuration article lists Enable IPv6 for Internet & SaaS and Enable IPv6 for Zscaler Client Connector.

quotes: When a test target resolves to an IPv6 address, ZDX traces the end-to-end path, measuring latency, packet loss, and jitter across each IPv6 hop.
You can view dual-stack (IPv4 and IPv6) or IPv6-only configurations.

ZDX relies on Internet & SaaS to route and inspect IPv6 traffic for telemetry collection and for clients inside a location. ZDX relies on Zscaler Client Connector to forward and detect IPv6 traffic for clients outside a location.
Enable IPv6 for Internet & SaaS.
Enable IPv6 for Zscaler Client Connector.

hop-view-tier.statement: The subscription table lists the Hop View (Granular Expanded Cloud Path) as supported on Standard, Microsoft 365, Advanced and Advanced Plus (columns in the order of the table's header row).

quotes: | Hop View (Granular Expanded Cloud Path) | Supported | Supported | Supported | Supported |
| Feature | Standard | Microsoft 365 | Advanced | Advanced Plus |

error-levels.statement: Cloud Path errors show as icons under the hop in the Hop View and next to the IP address in the Command Line View, at three levels: informational (no action required), warning (action might be necessary to achieve accurate Cloud Path results) and critical (an issue that could affect the user experience).

quotes: In the Hop View, the icons are displayed under the hop, while in the Command Line View, icons are displayed next to the IP address.
This message is for informational purposes only. No action is required.
This is a warning message. This indicates that action might be necessary to resolve an issue and achieve accurate Cloud Path results.
This is a critical error. This indicates an issue that could affect the user experience.

client-errors.statement: Client and reachability errors: a Client Connector internal error (contact Zscaler Support); a network communication failure, where an interface is down, probes get no response or ISP upstream connectivity might be down (verify ISP connectivity and that the probe's ICMP or UDP protocol is not blocked); an invalid or unresolvable domain (verify the domain name or DNS configuration); a failed proxy connection (verify the proxy policy, authentication and that access is allowed for the application URL); and an invalid HTTP URL in the Web probe.

quotes: | Zscaler Client Connector error. Contact Zscaler Support. | There is an internal error incurred by the Zscaler Client Connector. | Contact Zscaler Support. |

| Network communication failure. Either network interface is down or traffic is blocked. | There is a network error. One of the interfaces is down, the probes are not receiving a response, or the ISP upstream connectivity might be down. |
Verify your ISP connectivity and that the ICMP/UDP protocol configured for the probe is not blocked on the network.
| The domain is invalid or not resolvable. Verify your domain. | The domain is invalid or not resolvable. | Verify the name of the domain or your DNS configuration. |
| Proxy connection failed. | There were issues when connecting to your web proxy. | Verify your proxy policy and authentication mechanism and that access is allowed for this application URL. |
| Invalid HTTP URL. Check the Web probe configuration. | Connection to the host is successful, but there are issues with connecting to your URL. | Verify that your URL for the Web probe is correct. |

discarded-on-network-change.statement: A probe result is discarded when the network changes during the Cloud Path run: the sample's Cloud Path probes were aborted, Client Connector detected the change, and no action is required.

quotes: | The probe result was discarded due to a device network change. | The network changed during the Cloud Path probe run. Cloud Path probes for that sample were aborted. | Zscaler Client Connector detected the network change. No action is required. |

egress-errors.statement: Client egress errors: when the egress IP is tunneled the path to the client egress cannot be traced correctly (configure an access list on the router or SD-WAN device to bypass ICMP or UDP from the GRE or IPSec tunnel for the egress IP); when Client Connector cannot fetch ZDX service data from the Zscaler cloud the path to the egress cannot be traced and end-to-end latency does not include the client-to-egress latency (contact Zscaler Support); when egress detection fails with the configured protocol, try ICMP or UDP; and when the egress router does not answer Cloud Path probes from the ZIA Public Service Edge with an ICMP TTL expired message, configure it to return ICMP TTL expired messages for packets with IP TTL 1.

quotes: | The network path to the client egress cannot be traced. Configuring a GRE/IPSec tunnel bypass rule for the client egress router is recommended. | The network path to the client egress IP address cannot be traced correctly because the egress IP is tunneled.
Configure an access list for your router or SD-WAN device to bypass ICMP/UDP from the tunnel (GRE/IPSec) for your client egress IP address.
| The network path to the client egress cannot be traced. Zscaler Client Connector was unable to fetch ZDX service data from Zscaler cloud. |
This also means that the end-to-end latency value does not include the latency from the client to the internet egress point. | Contact Zscaler Support. |

| Client egress detection was not possible with the configured protocol type in the Cloud Path. Try a different protocol type. | The Zscaler Client Connector could not discover the user's Internet egress IP address. |
Verify the configuration and try a different protocol (ICMP/UDP). The current Cloud Path protocol is blocked.

| The client egress router did not respond to Cloud Path probes coming from the ZIA Public Service Edge. | The egress could not be probed. It did not respond with an ICMP TTL expired message for the ZDX Cloud Path probe. | Configure the router to return ICMP TTL expired messages for packets with IP TTL1. |

edge-protocol-errors.statement: Service Edge and protocol errors: ZDX does not collect hop information from the ZPA Public Service Edge to the application (no action required); a Public Service Edge unreachable from Client Connector means the TCP traceroute to it was dropped (check the network connection); ICMP and UDP probes are not supported in a No Default Route (NDR) environment (run probes via TCP); and traceroute packets not reaching the Zscaler Service Edge mean the ICMP, TCP or UDP protocol traceroute might not be supported on the network (ensure the network permits the configured protocol).

quotes: | Hop information from ZPA Public Service Edge to the application is not collected by ZDX. | We are not able to display the actual Cloud Path for applications accessed through Private Access. | No action required. |
| The Zscaler Public Service Edge is not reachable from Zscaler Client Connector. | The TCP traceroute to the Zscaler Service Edge was dropped. | Check your network connection. |
| Probe not allowed in NDR. | ICMP and UDP probes are not supported in a No Default Route (NDR) environment. | Ensure you're running probes via TCP. |

| Traceroute packets are not reaching the Zscaler Service Edge. | ICMP, TCP, or UDP protocol traceroute might not be supported on the network. | Ensure the underlying network permits the configured protocol. |

external-proxy-errors.statement: External proxy errors: the legs from the external proxy to the destination, to the egress or to the data center egress, and from the data center egress or the egress to the destination when an external proxy is present, are not discoverable (path not available, no action required); Cloud Path packets not reaching the external proxy mean the ICMP protocol might not be supported on the network (ensure it allows ICMP packets).

quotes: | Data from external proxy to destination is not discoverable. | Path is not available. | No action required. |
| Data from external proxy to egress is not discoverable. | Path is not available. | No action required. |
| Cloud Path packets are not reaching the external proxy. | ICMP protocol might not be supported on the network. | Ensure the underlying network allows ICMP packets. |
| Data from external proxy to data center egress is not discoverable. | Path is not available. | No action required. |
| Data from data center egress to destination is not discoverable when external proxy is present. | Path is not available. | No action required. |
| Data from egress to destination is not discoverable when external proxy is present. | Path is not available. | No action required. |

pa-errors.statement: ZDX can report Private Access errors from the Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge for Private Access: an internal error and an unreachable application (contact Zscaler Support); a failure to retrieve customer information (ask the user to reauthenticate, and contact Support if it persists); an expired user session, where a data connection cannot be set up because reauthentication is required; and a failure to fill assistant groups due to a configuration error (ask the user to validate configuration).

quotes: ZDX can report error codes for the following Private Access errors. These errors are applicable to either the Public Service Edge for Private Access or Private Service Edge for Private Access component.
| ZPA internal error. | The probe might have encountered a Private Access internal error. | Contact Zscaler Support. |
| ZPA application is not reachable. | The probe might have failed to reach the Private Access destination. | Contact Zscaler Support. |

| Error in finding customer. | The Public Service Edge for Private Access or Private Service Edge for Private Access cannot retrieve customer information due to a configuration error when processing the data connection request. | Ask the user to reauthenticate. If the error persists, contact Zscaler Support. |
| User session expired. | The Public Service Edge for Private Access or Private Service Edge for Private Access cannot set up a data connection because reauthentication is required. |

| Error in filling assistant groups. | The Public Service Edge for Private Access or Private Service Edge for Private Access cannot fill assistant groups due to a configuration error when processing the data request. | Ask the user to validate configuration.

pa-policy-errors.statement: Private Access policy errors: no valid policy matches the application request (a missing or mismatched setting in policy, SAML or SCIM attributes, Posture Profiles, Trusted Networks, Client Types, Cloud Connector Groups or Machine Groups, or a disabled App Segment or App Group Segment); no App Connector group in the Server group (edit the Server group to add them); the application policy or the timeout policy blocked the request (the user is not allowed, or must reauthenticate in Client Connector); the application is not configured; and a connection request timed out waiting for a data connection request from an App Connector (ensure the App Connectors can reach the edge and the application).

quotes: | Policy or attributes misconfigured for access. | A valid policy cannot be matched to an application access request. There is a missing or mismatched configuration in policy settings, SAML/SCIM attributes, Posture Profiles, Trusted Networks, Client Types, Cloud Connector Groups, or Machine Groups.
The application request is also blocked when an App Segment or App Group Segment is disabled.

| App Connector group not configured. | The Public Service Edge for Private Access was unable to process the application request since an App Connector group was not specified in the Server group configuration. | Edit the Server group to add the App Connector groups.

| Application policy blocked access. | The Private Access service blocked the application request because the user isn't allowed to access the requested application. | Update the policy to allow the user access. |

| Timeout policy blocked access. | The Private Access service blocked the application request because the timeout policy requires the user to authenticate. | The user must reauthenticate in Zscaler Client Connector. |
| Application not configured. | The Public Service Edge for Private Access or the Private Service Edge for Private Access cannot set up a connection since the application is not configured. |

| Connection request timed out. | The Public Service Edge for Private Access or Private Service Edge for Private Access was waiting for a data connection request from an App Connector that could provide access to the application, but the request timed out while waiting.
Ensure that the App Connectors can reach the Public Service Edge for Private Access or Private Service Edge for Private Access and the requested application. |
